segments.headline: DON'T GIVE AN AGENT YOUR KEYS
segments.body: An AI agent should not approve and send payments alone.
segments.spoken: Your AI agent should not be able to approve and send a payment without an independent check.

segments.headline: READ FIRST
segments.body: Start with read-only access. Separate every write permission.
segments.spoken: Gate one: start with read-only access. Give each workflow only the specific write permissions it needs.

segments.headline: HUMAN APPROVAL
segments.body: Payments, deletions and external messages need checkpoints.
segments.spoken: Gate two: require independent human approval before payments, destructive changes, or other high-impact actions.

segments.headline: LOG AND REVOKE
segments.body: Record tool, actor, action, approval and outcome.
segments.spoken: Gate three: record every action and approval. Keep a simple way to revoke access and stop the workflow.

segments.headline: TRY A BAD INSTRUCTION
segments.body: See whether untrusted content can trigger an unauthorized action.
segments.spoken: Then test with a misleading document. If an embedded instruction can bypass those controls, do not deploy the agent with production authority.

segments.headline: CONTROL THE PERMISSIONS
segments.body: A system prompt is not a substitute for access controls.
segments.spoken: These are practical management safeguards, not a universal legal checklist. PrismBay AI explains AI systems founders and operators can govern.
